title: Shannon entropy and genome size
legend: Dominant-superfamily evenness tends to decline with genome size across the 21 overlapping species. Twenty-one species with both genome-size and repeat-diversity data are shown in each panel. (a) Shannon entropy and (b) Gini–Simpson index summarize each species' ten most abundant positive classified dnaPipeTE superfamilies, reclosed to sum to one. These related measures represent diversity/evenness of the selected superfamily distribution, not total TE burden or independent replications. Points identify reproductive strategy; horizontal bars show genome-size measurement intervals. All observations contribute to the same full-sample fit per panel. Lines and bands reuse stored Pagel-lambda PGLS fitted means and 95% coefficient intervals without refitting. The Shannon slope is −0.007558 per pg/1C (95% CI −0.015234–0.000118; P = 0.0533), and the Gini–Simpson slope is −0.003623 (−0.006964–−0.000283; P = 0.0350). Both fitted lambdas are 1. P values are unadjusted. Predictor measurement error and tree uncertainty are not propagated. D. aeneus, D. wrighti and D. valtos are labelled in the collage to identify the genome-size extremes and the high-diversity direct developer; label selection does not change the 21-species sample. All 21 species are individually named in isolated panels. Genome size is based on nuclear integrated optical density (IOD), anchored to the D. fuscus assembly scale. Measurement intervals exclude anchor uncertainty; run-specific calibration remains unresolved. Sizes are species summaries, not independently validated C-values. Abbreviations: TE, transposable element; PGLS, phylogenetic generalized least squares; CI, confidence interval.
